# chip-macro-placement-search -- setting "set_a".
#
# Four processes, and the split is what makes the budget real:
#
#   stage   root, isolated interpreter -- resolves this setting's chip and its
#           evaluation budget through the HELD-OUT index.json, copies the chip's
#           netlist into $OUT/priv (root, 0700) and writes the policy-visible
#           meta.json (macro count, grid, budget) into $OUT/work.
#   oracle  root -- owns the netlist, the FIXED wire-mask decoder + cal_hpwl, and
#           the budget counter (plus a pool of forked decoder workers for
#           batched requests), and starts the policy as an unprivileged CHILD
#           with an empty environment.
#           A layout's HPWL reaches the policy only as the answer to one request
#           over that pipe, and only while the count is under budget.
#   policy  unprivileged, inside the oracle -- imports search_policy.py and calls
#           search(ctx).  The netlist file is unreadable to this uid, so the only
#           way to a low HPWL is to route candidates through the host-run decoder.
#   score   root, isolated interpreter -- reads the oracle's result log and turns
#           it into the scored line, in a process the policy has already exited
#           from and which never imports its module.
#
# The five fixed harness scripts are executed from an immutable COPY taken before
# any candidate code could run, whose sha256 this shell re-checks before every
# use: the workspace is writable by whoever owns the container, so running the
# fixed scripts out of it would let a submission rewrite its own scorer -- or its
# own budget counter.
#
# The single scored line is relayed from this shell after every Python process
# has exited, followed by MLSBENCH_TERMINAL_OK as the very last line.
set -euo pipefail

LABEL="${ENV:-set_a}"
SEED="${SEED:-42}"

SETTING="$LABEL"
MAX_POLICY_BYTES=65536
RUN_TIMEOUT="${WIREMASK_RUN_TIMEOUT:-21600}"
# The unprivileged uid is unique per (setting, seed): all six settings run
# concurrently in one container (config.json puts them in one group), and this
# script's own `pkill -9 -u` / `find -uid ... -delete` sweep must never touch
# another run's policy.  A numeric uid needs no passwd entry.
UID_BASE=27648
case "$SETTING" in
    set_a) SIDX=0 ;; set_b) SIDX=1 ;; set_c) SIDX=2 ;;
    set_d) SIDX=3 ;; set_e) SIDX=4 ;; set_f) SIDX=5 ;;
    *) printf 'INVALID: unknown setting %s\n' "$SETTING"; exit 1 ;;
esac
RUNUID=$((UID_BASE + SIDX * 512 + SEED % 512))
RUNGID="$RUNUID"

WS=/workspace/wiremask-bbo/mlsplace
OUT="${OUTPUT_DIR:-/tmp/wiremask_out}/${LABEL}-${SEED}"
THREADS="${WIREMASK_THREADS:-4}"
# One policy per SETTING runs at a time (see the lock below) and the six
# settings run side by side, so each policy gets ~1/6 of the container:
# 5 decoders and 4 BLAS/torch threads.
# Parallel decoders the oracle forks (root, before the policy exists) for
# ctx.evaluate_batch.  Fixed here, not by the policy: it changes wall time only
# -- the budget counts candidates and a batch decodes exactly as one-by-one.
WORKERS="${WIREMASK_DECODE_WORKERS:-5}"

if [ "$(id -u)" != "0" ]; then
    printf 'INVALID: this evaluation drops privileges to keep the netlist out of the policy process and therefore needs a root container\n'
    exit 1
fi

rm -rf "$OUT"
mkdir -p "$OUT/work" "$OUT/priv"
chmod 755 "$OUT"
chown 0:0 "$OUT/priv"
chmod 700 "$OUT/priv"
find "$WS" -maxdepth 2 -name '__pycache__' -type d -prune -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
find "$WS" -maxdepth 2 -name '*.pyc' -delete 2>/dev/null || true

HARNESS=$(mktemp -d)
# One lock per setting: a policy of another setting may run concurrently -- it
# decodes a different chip (different n_macros), so nothing it could share is
# worth a decode here -- but never two seeds of the same chip.
LOCK="/run/mlsb-chip-macro-policy-$SETTING.lock"
sweep_uid() {
    pkill -9 -u "$RUNUID" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do pgrep -u "$RUNUID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || break; sleep 0.2; done
    awk '$3 !~ /^(proc|sysfs|cgroup2?|devpts|devtmpfs|mqueue_none)$/ {print $2}' /proc/mounts \
        | sort -u | while read -r mp; do
            find "$mp" -xdev -uid "$RUNUID" -depth -delete 2>/dev/null || true
        done
    for kind in shm:m msg:q sem:s; do
        f=/proc/sysvipc/${kind%%:*}

        awk -v u="$RUNUID" 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="uid") c=i; next} c && $c==u {print $2}' "$f" \
            | while read -r id; do
                # IPC_RMID needs the owner's uid (or CAP_SYS_ADMIN, which a
                # container does not have): remove it AS the owner.
                setpriv --reuid="$RUNUID" --regid="$RUNUID" --clear-groups \
                    ipcrm "-${kind##*:}" "$id" 2>/dev/null || true
            done
    done
}
cleanup() {
    sweep_uid
    rm -rf "$HARNESS" "$OUT"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
cp "$WS/search_data.py" "$WS/search_stage.py" "$WS/search_server.py" \
   "$WS/search_client.py" "$WS/search_score.py" "$HARNESS/"
chmod 755 "$HARNESS"
chmod 644 "$HARNESS"/*.py
declare -A SHA
for f in search_data search_stage search_server search_client search_score; do
    SHA[$f]=$(sha256sum "$HARNESS/$f.py" | cut -d' ' -f1)
done
verify() {
    if [ "$(sha256sum "$HARNESS/$1.py" | cut -d' ' -f1)" != "${SHA[$1]}" ]; then
        printf 'INVALID: the fixed harness was modified during the run (%s)\n' "$1"
        exit 1
    fi
}

policy_bytes=$(stat -c %s "$WS/search_policy.py")
if [ "$policy_bytes" -gt "$MAX_POLICY_BYTES" ]; then
    printf 'INVALID: search_policy.py is %d bytes, over the %d byte limit for this file\n' \
        "$policy_bytes" "$MAX_POLICY_BYTES"

# launcher (-I -S -B, explicit site path, no cwd / script dir on sys.path, no
# site hooks) when the verifier provides it; natively the previous flags.
read -r -a TPY <<< "${MLSBENCH_TRUSTED_PYTHON:-python3 -P -B -E -s}"

STRIP='/^[[:space:]]*TEST_METRICS:/d; /^[[:space:]]*FINAL_TEST_METRICS:/d; /^[[:space:]]*MLSBENCH_TERMINAL_OK[[:space:]]*$/d'

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- stage
verify search_stage
set +e
stage_out=$("${TPY[@]}" "$HARNESS/search_stage.py" \
    --setting "$SETTING" --outdir "$OUT" 2>&1)
rc=$?
set -e
printf '%s\n' "$stage_out" | sed "$STRIP"
if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then printf 'INVALID: input staging exited with status %d\n' "$rc"; exit "$rc"; fi

chown -R "$RUNUID:$RUNGID" "$OUT/work"
chmod 700 "$OUT/work"

# ------------------------------------------------------- oracle + policy
# ONE POLICY PER CHIP AT A TIME, container-wide.  A setting's seeds are started
# concurrently in one container, and without namespaces (no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no
# user namespaces under Docker's seccomp -- measured) two policy uids can talk:
# /tmp, /var/tmp, /run/lock, /dev/shm and /dev/mqueue are 1777, SysV IPC
# objects can be created 0666, and loopback sockets work.  Measured:
# seed 42's uid wrote /dev/shm/pool_seed42 and seed 123's uid read it, and
# "every seed reports the global best" scored ea 0.5296 vs 0.4931 honest --
# five budgets pooled into one.  So the policy phase runs under an exclusive
# lock, and before the lock is released every process of this seed's uid is
# killed and everything it owns is removed from every writable filesystem and
# from SysV IPC.  The next seed's policy starts in a container that holds
# nothing from this one.  (Stage and score stay outside the lock: no
# submission code runs in them.)

verify search_client
verify search_server

flock 9
t0=$(date +%s%N)
set +e

# leaves behind inherits the stream, and $( ) would wait for it forever while
# holding the lock.
timeout -s KILL "$((RUN_TIMEOUT + 120))" \
    "${TPY[@]}" "$HARNESS/search_server.py" --outdir "$OUT" \
        --client "$HARNESS/search_client.py" --policy "$WS/search_policy.py" \
        --seed "$SEED" --threads "$THREADS" --workers "$WORKERS" \
        --uid "$RUNUID" --timeout "$RUN_TIMEOUT" > "$OUT/priv/run.log" 2>&1
rc=$?
set -e
t1=$(date +%s%N)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------- sweep
sweep_uid
flock -u 9
exec 9>&-
sed "$STRIP" "$OUT/priv/run.log"
if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then printf 'INVALID: the search process exited with status %d\n' "$rc"; exit "$rc"; fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- score
verify search_score
set +e
score_out=$("${TPY[@]}" "$HARNESS/search_score.py" --outdir "$OUT" \
    --elapsed-ns "$((t1 - t0))" 2>&1)
rc=$?
set -e

if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then printf 'INVALID: scoring exited with status %d\n' "$rc"; exit "$rc"; fi

if [ "$count" -ne 1 ]; then printf 'INVALID: expected exactly one TEST_METRICS line (found %s)\n' "$count"; exit 1; fi

# ONLY this root-only file, which no policy uid can open.
